title: Exceptions check
instructions: Five questions on try, except and raise.

questions.explanation: The text cannot be converted to a number, so Python raises a ValueError.

questions.prompt: In a try block, an error happens on line 2 of 4. What happens to lines 3 and 4?
options: They are skipped, and Python jumps to a matching except
questions.explanation: The rest of the try block is abandoned as soon as the exception is raised.

questions.prompt: When does a finally block run?
options: Only if there was an error
Only if there was no error
questions.explanation: finally runs whether or not an exception happened, which makes it the place for clean-up.

questions.prompt: Why is `except Exception: pass` usually a bad idea?
options: It hides real bugs, because errors vanish without a trace
questions.explanation: Silencing every error means you never find out something is broken. Handle specific errors and say something useful.

options: Raises a ValueError with that message
questions.explanation: raise creates and throws the exception yourself, so your function can refuse bad input.

title: Safe helpers
instructions:
Write two functions that never crash:

- `safe_int(text, default=0)` returns `int(text)`, or `default` if the text is not a valid number.
- `safe_divide(a, b)` returns `a / b`, or `None` if `b` is zero.

Catch only the exceptions you expect. There is nothing to print.

title: Order the try block
instructions: Put the lines in order so the program prints `not a number`. The indentation is part of each line.
